chapter.title: Interactions and Async
chapter.description: Simulating real user behaviour and waiting for the result.

blocks.text: `user-event` simulates what a real interaction does: focus, keydown, keypress, input, keyup, change. `fireEvent` dispatches a single raw event, which often misses behaviour your component depends on.
Every `user-event` method returns a promise. Forgetting `await` produces tests that pass by accident and fail intermittently in CI.
Do not put multiple assertions inside one `waitFor`. It retries the whole callback, so a failure in the first assertion hides the rest and the error message becomes useless.

'An update to X was not wrapped in act(...)' almost always means a state update happened after the test finished - usually an unawaited promise. The fix is nearly always an `await`, not wrapping things in `act` yourself.

previous.title: Queries
previous.description: Finding elements the way a user would, in priority order.

blocks.text: Testing Library offers many queries, and the order you should prefer them in is deliberate: the higher up the list, the closer it is to how a real user finds things.

items: `getByRole` - the way assistive technology sees the page. Almost always the right choice.
`getByLabelText` - for form fields, and it verifies the label is correctly associated.
`getByPlaceholderText` - when there is genuinely no label.
`getByTestId` - the escape hatch, when nothing else identifies the element.

blocks.text: Using `getByRole` pushes you towards accessible markup, because an element with no role or accessible name is hard to query - and equally hard for a screen reader user to use.

items: `getBy...` - throws if not found. Use when the element should be there.
`queryBy...` - returns `null` if not found. The only one to use for asserting absence.
`findBy...` - returns a promise and retries. Use for anything that appears asynchronously.

blocks.text: Using `getBy` to assert something is absent fails with a confusing 'unable to find element' error instead of a clean assertion failure. Reach for `queryBy` every time you expect nothing.

next.title: Mocking and Setup
next.description: Faking the network, testing hooks, and a checklist for good tests.

blocks.text: Mocking `fetch` by hand couples your tests to how the request is made. Mock Service Worker intercepts at the network level, so the component uses its real data layer.
Test a hook directly only when it is a reusable utility. A hook that exists for one component is better tested through that component, where the assertions describe real behaviour.

items: Query by role first; fall back to test ids only when nothing else works.
Use `queryBy` for absence, `findBy` for anything asynchronous.
Mock at the network boundary, not at the module boundary.
One behaviour per test, with a name that says what the user should see.
If a refactor breaks a test but not the app, rewrite the test.

blocks.title: Choose the right query type
blocks.instructions: Complete queryFor so it returns 'findBy' for async, 'queryBy' for absence checks, and 'getBy' otherwise.
